This is an application for condonation of delay in  preferring the appeal under Section 173 of the Motor  Vehicles Act, 1988, read with Section 5 of the  Limitation Act.

Mr Jayanta Banerjee, learned Advocate for  appellants-claimants submits, at the outset, that the  learned tribunal instead of directing the insurance  company to pay and recover in a case of breach of  condition of policy of insurance has directed the owner  of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation and  thus the appeal involves a substantial question of law  as to propriety of such direction in view of settled  position of law.

sentences.text: Moreover, due to Covid-pandemic in the early part of 2020, neither the appellants-claimants could procure certified copy of the impugned judgment and award from learned Tribunal nor could file appeal during such period.

He fairly submits though at the first instance he submitted before the court that execution proceedings were initiated by the claimants but after thorough searching of the records he found that no such execution proceedings was filed by the claimants before the learned tribunal.

Furthermore, he submits that every days delay is not required to be explained,
and a rational approach should be made while deciding the application for condonation of delay.

In support of his condonation he relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in Collector, Land Acquisition, Anant Nag and Anr. versus Mst. Katiji and Ors. reported in AIR 1987 SUPREME COURT 1353.

sentences.text: The aforesaid application for condonation of delay has been keenly contested by respondent No. 1 Insurance Company by filing affidavit-in-opposition.

Mr Rajdeep Bhattacharyya, learned Advocate for insurance company submits that although liberal approach is to be given while dealing with an application for condonation of delay but where there is dearth of proper explanation regarding such delay that should be deprecated.

He indicates that in the application for condonation of delay since passing of the award on 14th November, 2017 till the second week of March, 2020 there is no such reasonable explanation made by the appellants-claimants in support of delay in preferring the appeal during such period.
In support of his contention he relies on a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in N. Balakrishnan versus M. Krishnamurthy reported in (1998)7 Supreme Court Cases 123.

entities.text: N. Balakrishnan versus M. Krishnamurthy reported in (1998)7 Supreme Court Cases 123
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that in the event the court decides the application in favour of the appellants-claimants there should be imposition of cost upon the appellants.
Inspite of service of copy of application for condonation of delay, respondent no.2-owner of the offending vehicle is unrepresented.
Having heard the learned advocates for respective parties, I now proceed to decide the rival contentions of the parties in the present application.
As per report of Additional Stamp Reporter dated 14 June 2022, there is delay of 864 days in preferring the appeal.

Be that as it may, upon going through the memorandum of appeal it is found that the appellants- claimants have challenged the propriety of the order of the learned tribunal directing the owner of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation amount instead of applying the principles of pay and recovery upon the insurance company.
In N. Balakrishnan (supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the primary function of a court is to adjudicate the dispute between the parties and to advance substantial justice.
The time-limit fixed for approaching the court in different situations is not because on the expiry of such time a bad cause would transform into a good cause.
It further observed that rules of limitation are not meant to destroy the rights of parties.
They are meant to see that parties do not resort to dilatory tactics but seek their remedy promptly.

In Collector, Land Acquisition, Anant Nag (supra) the Hon'ble Court observed that when substantial justice and technical considerations are pitted against each other cause of substantial justice deserves to be preferred for the other side cannot claim to have vested right in injustice being done because of a non- deliberate delay.

sentences.text: Bearing in mind the aforesaid observations of the Hon'ble Court, since the appellants-claimants have raised a substantial question whether principles of pay and recovery upon the insurance company is applicable in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am to inclined to condone the delay of 864 days in preferring the appeal.
Accordingly such delay stands condoned.
The application being CAN 1 of 2022 stands disposed of.
The appeal is formally admitted and registered.

This appeal is preferred against the judgment and award dated 14th November, 2017 passed by learned Judge Motor Vehicles Claims Tribunal, first court, Paschim Medinipur in MAC Case No. 372 of 2014, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: Call for the Lower Court Records.
Department is directed to take effective steps for bringing the lower courts record from the learned Tribunal within a two weeks from the date.

Upon receipt of the lower court records the office shall examine the same and if found to be complete and in order shall serve notice of arrival of lower court records upon learned Advocate for appellants- claimants as well as the learned Advocate for respondent no. 1 Insurance Company.

Upon receipt of notice of arrival of lower court records learned Advocate for appellants-claimants shall prepare and file requisite numbers of informal paper books incorporating all relevant papers and documents including pleadings and evidence, both oral and documentary, in printed or cyclostyle or type written form within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of notice of arrival of lower court records.
Appellants-claimants is directed to deposit talabana cost together with written up notice forms for causing service of notice of appeal upon respondent No. 2-owner of the offending vehicle.
Since the respondent No. 1-Insurance Company has already entered appearance service of notice of appeal upon the said respondent is dispensed with.
Matter to go out of list with liberty to mention.
(Bivas Pattanayak, J)
